title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Two defects in the dead-code family, found by auditing it against its own promise
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.1 fixes two defects found by attacking the dead-code checks rather than trusting them. One turned every check off for a file that merely quoted @file:Suppress in a comment or a string, silently. The other invented a declaration the parser never meant as one, and in Find Dead Islands that phantom took a live class down with it. Both were reproduced on the kotlin-lsp repository before the fix, and measured on it after.

highlights.title: @file:Suppress is read in the header, and nowhere else
highlights.description: The annotation used to be matched anywhere in the raw file, so a mention inside a KDoc, a string literal or a commented-out TODO turned every dead-code check off for that file, with nothing logged and nothing reported. It is now read above package only, where Kotlin requires it. Nested block comments count as comments, and packageName no longer passes for the start of the body. Two spellings that were being ignored are honoured now: @file:[JvmName("X") Suppress("unused")] and @file:kotlin.Suppress("unused").

highlights.title: An anonymous object is not a dead declaration
highlights.description: The parser names object : Base { } as $anon$<line> so it can count anonymous implementors. At file scope that synthetic name reached the unreferenced-symbol scan, where no word in any file can ever match it, so it walked through every guard. On the kotlin-lsp repository it produced one phantom finding, and Find Dead Islands reported it as an island together with LSJavaHoverProvider, a live class it dragged in.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The five per-file detectors (unused imports, parameters, private declarations, locals, write-only variables) moved into modules that do not import vscode, so they can run outside the editor. Behaviour is unchanged: on 659 files, all 279 findings and the edits of every quick fix are byte for byte what they were.
A command line harness now runs those five over a whole project. They had never been measured on a corpus.
